- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots — cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +5% below peak.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-period (e.g., +0.3+), model frequently overreacts — dampen forecast slope for next 5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecast days are above 80, true price often pulls back — adjust downward by 2–5% per day.
- Forecast horizon 30d: if sentiment is consistently negative, model tends to overestimate recovery — reduce final 5–7 days’ forecast by 3–6%.
- Lagged sentiment: if sentiment was negative 3–5 days ago, model often misses downward correction — adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to reflect sentiment lag.
